projects.title: Gender Gaps in Life Expectancy
projects.description: Technical reports for an analysis of why women outlive men in OECD countries: a Bayesian panel model, counterfactuals, data, and code.

children.title: 1. The Gender Gap in Life Expectancy

pages.title: Gender Gaps in Life Expectancy: Why Do Women Live Longer Than Men?
pages.description: Why do women live longer than men? A summary of what drives the life expectancy gender gap in OECD countries, and the policies that could narrow it.

pages.title: Blog Series
The Gender Gap in Life Expectancy
pages.short_title: 1. The Gender Gap in Life Expectancy
pages.description: The gender gap in life expectancy ranges from 2.5 to 12.7 years across OECD countries and has shrunk over time, so it is not natural or inevitable.

pages.title: What Drives the Life Expectancy Gender Gap?
pages.description: Which causes of death drive the life expectancy gender gap? A Bayesian panel model of the gaps in road traffic, suicide, homicide, and drug deaths.

pages.title: How Much of the Life Expectancy Gap Could We Close?
pages.description: How much of the US life expectancy gender gap could close if deaths from road traffic, drugs, suicide, and homicide fell to the best observed levels?

pages.title: International Patterns: Policies and Prevention
pages.description: The leading causes of the life expectancy gender gap by OECD country and region, and policy lessons from road safety in Europe, alcohol, and violence.

pages.title: Healthy Life Expectancy and the Gender Gap
pages.description: The gender gap in healthy life expectancy (HALE): which causes of death drive it, how it compares with life expectancy, and counterfactuals for the US.

pages.title: Methods and Results
Bayesian Panel Data Model: Analysis of HALE and Life Expectancy Gender Gaps (Extended Through 2023 with IHME HALE)
pages.description: A Bayesian hierarchical panel model of the life expectancy and HALE gender gaps in OECD countries, 2000 to 2023: coefficients, fit, and counterfactuals.

pages.title: Causal framing and CausalPy Models 1 / 1b / 1c: results note
pages.description: Causal diagrams (DAGs) for the life expectancy gap model, fixed-effects regressions that implement them, and a comparison with the Bayesian estimates.

pages.title: Model Validation: Replacing WHO Indicators with IHME Indicators
pages.description: Validation experiments: replacing WHO indicators with IHME indicators one at a time to check that conclusions about the gender gap are stable.

pages.title: Data Inventory
pages.description: Data sources for the life expectancy gender gap analysis: IHME Global Burden of Disease, Our World in Data, and WHO indicators, with download settings.

pages.title: Python to R: The Same Bayesian Model in PyMC and brms
pages.description: The same Bayesian hierarchical model written in Python with PyMC and in R with brms, and a comparison showing that the two posteriors agree.

pages.title: Archive: Working Notes
Bayesian Panel Data Model: Analysis of HALE and Life Expectancy Gender Gaps (Extended Through 2021 with COVID-19)
pages.description: An earlier version of the Bayesian panel model of the life expectancy and HALE gender gaps, using WHO data for 2000 to 2021 and COVID-19 deaths.

pages.title: Exploratory Data Analysis: Summary Report
pages.description: Exploratory data analysis of the life expectancy and HALE gender gaps in OECD countries, and of the cause-specific death rates used as predictors.

pages.title: Time Series Analysis: Trends in Health Indicators and Gender Gaps (2000-2023)
pages.description: Trends in the life expectancy and HALE gender gaps in OECD countries, and in cause-specific death rates for men and women, from 2000 to 2023.

pages.title: Temporal Analysis: Evolution of Health Patterns Over Time
pages.description: How the factors that explain the life expectancy gender gap changed over time, from cross-sectional models fit at five-year intervals, 2000 to 2019.

pages.title: Gender Gaps in Life Expectancy
pages.description: Cross-sectional Elastic Net regression models of the gender gaps in life expectancy and HALE, which came before the Bayesian panel model.

pages.title: Neoplasms Drilldown Analysis Report
pages.description: The gender gap in cancer mortality in the US, Iceland, and the OECD, broken down by cancer type and by behavioral, metabolic, and environmental risks.
